questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 ?
questions.explain: Count the 10s: there are 3 of them, so this is 3 groups of 10, which is 3 × 10 = 30. Counting one group too few gives 2 × 10, which is 10 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 10 × 10 or 2 × 3. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Jun Hao works out 1810 + 1976 in columns. One column makes 17, so he writes 7 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 7 he writes there worth?
questions.stemText: Jun Hao works out 1810 + 1976 in columns. One column makes 17, so he writes 7 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 7 he writes there worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 17 is the hundreds column: 8 + 9 = 17, and no other column reaches ten. 17 hundreds is 1 thousand and 7 hundreds, so the 7 stays in the hundreds column - worth 700 - and the small 1 goes above the thousands column - worth 1000. The 7 is worth 700. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stem: Mei Ling works out 82 + 83 in her head. She makes 90 first. 82 + 83 = 90 + ?
questions.stemText: Mei Ling works out 82 + 83 in her head. She makes 90 first. 82 + 83 = 90 + ?
questions.explain: To get from 83 up to 90 you need 7, so 7 is moved across from the 82. That leaves 82 − 7 = 75, and 90 + 75 = 165. Whatever you give to one number you must take off the other, or the total changes. You could have rounded the 82 up to 90 instead and taken that amount off the 83: it is the same total either way, so it lands on the same answer.

questions.stemText: Siti works out 5623 − 2138. In every column she takes the smaller digit away from the bigger one, and gets 3515. What is the correct answer?
questions.explain: Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column ignores which number is on top, and that is how 3515 appears. questions.stemText: Priya had some stamps. She gave away 701 of them, then bought 349 more. Now she has 3498. How many stamps did she have at first?

questions.stemText: Xin Yi is thinking of a 4-digit number. These are her clues: • The hundreds digit is 2. • All its digits are different. • The ones digit is 4 more than the tens digit. • The thousands digit is 9. What is the greatest number it can be?
questions.explain: Write down the digits you are told: the thousands digit is 9 and the hundreds digit is 2. The ones digit is 4 more than the tens digit, so list every pair that works: tens 0 and ones 4; tens 1 and ones 5; tens 2 and ones 6; tens 3 and ones 7; tens 4 and ones 8; tens 5 and ones 9. (With tens 6, the ones digit would be 10, which is not a digit.) So the number could be 9204, 9215, 9226, 9237, 9248 or 9259. All its digits are different, so cross out 9226 and 9259 (each has a digit twice). That leaves 9204, 9215, 9237 and 9248. The greatest of these is 9248. (Without the last step you would choose 9259, but it breaks the clue “All its digits are different.”)

questions.stemText: At a bakery in Toa Payoh, packets of ang ku kueh cost $2 each, or 5 for $9. Xin Yi needs 13 packets of ang ku kueh. What is the least amount Xin Yi must pay? (in dollars, e.g. 4.75)
questions.explain: Buying 5 packets of ang ku kueh one by one costs 5 × $2 = $10, but 5 for $9 is cheaper, so buy as many bundles as you can. 13 ÷ 5 = 2 remainder 3, so 2 bundles cost 2 × $9 = $18. The 3 packets of ang ku kueh left over cost 3 × $2 = $6 (cheaper than one more bundle at $9). Total: $18 + $6 = $24. Buying all 13 one by one would cost $26.

questions.stemText: A watermelon is 3 times as heavy as a papaya. Together they weigh 3 kg 200 g. How much heavier is the watermelon than the papaya, in g?

questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 13 cm long and 6 cm wide. A notch 6 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 4 cm after it, and the banner is still 4 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 3 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 13 + 6 = 42 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 6 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 6 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (13 + 6) + 2 × 2 = 42 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
